La Passa is a procession of bachelors' couples through Sant Julià de Lòria, not a dance
Couples marrying that year lead and are called majors fadrins; remaining couples follow from older to younger
The procession makes marriage order and social age hierarchy publicly visible
Sant Antoni falls on 17 January and the animal blessing, rest and extra feed precede the communal meal
All parishes distribute escudella outdoors around mid-January
Canillo calls the dish vianda; its first popular edition was in 1979 at plaça de Montaup and now takes place on the Sunday nearest Sant Antoni with around one thousand servings
Encants are auctions; the tradition in Canillo was restored around 2000 by Josep Casal and the Comú
Andorran falles are spinning torches for Sant Joan, distinct from Valencian monuments
Historically, youths ran dark streets spinning birch-bark torches attached to boxwood sticks

The custom was revived around 1997-1998 after being lost; cotton with fuel and an association replaced bark and spontaneous youth participation because few birches remained and stripping bark would be an environmental offense
